§ 2Content

§ 3BODY LEVEL OF ORGANISATION

  • Body level organization refers to the hierarchical arrangement of structures within a living organism, from the smallest units to the entire organism. It involves five main levels: cells, tissues, organs, organ systems, and the organism.

The 5 Levels

  1. 1. Cell — the basic unit of life. See 01 - Cell.
  2. 2. Tissue — a group of similar cells performing a common function. See 02 - Plant Tissue and Animal Tissue.
  3. 3. Organ — a structure made of different tissues working together (e.g. heart, stomach, leaf).
  4. 4. Organ system — a group of organs working together for a common function (e.g. digestive system, circulatory system).
  5. 5. Organism — the complete living being.

Per-Phylum Examples (Animalia)

PhylumBody level
PoriferaCellular level (no true tissues)
Cnidaria / CoelenterataTissue level
PlatyhelminthesOrgan level
Annelida, Arthropoda, Mollusca, Echinodermata, ChordataOrgan system level

The progression from cellular → tissue → organ → organ system tracks increasing complexity across the animal kingdom.

§ 4Key concepts

  • 5 levels: cell → tissue → organ → organ system → organism
  • Porifera = cellular | Cnidaria = tissue | Platyhelminthes = organ | Annelida+ = organ system
